newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Spanish December CPI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Spanish December CPI data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to Spanish December consumer price data, which moderated as expected.
In December, prices rose 0.3 percent month-on-month, for a 3.2 percent year-on-year rate. The core rate rose 0.3 percent month-on-month for a 3.0 percent year-on-year rate.
Here are their comments:
KEN WATTRET, PARIBAS LONDON - RFTV
"The Bank of Spain may feel that another quarter-point cut in the short term would serve to keep the currency stable."
When asked whether the central bank might reduce its 6.25 percent money market rate at Thursday's regular repo, he said "It's a 50-50 call."
"In the very short term currency strength is likely to continue."
"I think there is a risk at some point that we do get a correction in this market..from these very bullish levels."
JUAN MIELGO, BANK OF AMERICA MADRID - RFTV
"It's clearly below the official forecast for 1996."
When asked whether there would be an interest rate cut on Thursday, he said "I don't think so. If they did, it would be...because of the peseta's appreciation."
"I think the market is more bullish than it should be from a fundamentals point of view."
GWYN HACCHE, HSBC JAMES CAPEL LONDON - RFTV
"Inflation in Spain will probably tip below three percent in January."

When asked whether there might be a rate cut tomorrow, he said, "It is quite a close call, but they cut fairly recently and my feeling is they will hold off until we get the fall in January inflation figures published in mid-February."
The bond market is pricing in too high a probability of Spain being in EMU, he added.
RICCARDO BARBIERI, MORGAN STANLEY INTERNATIONAL LONDON
"It's very good. We were expecting a decline in food and energy prices, but we are also seeing a decline in the core, which is a signal of the continuing downtrend."
"The strong peseta will also help to tame inflation.

"This could prod the Bank of Spain to a fresh rate cut of 25 basis points tomorrow, but it won't brake the bullishness in the market over short-term interest rates and it won't alleviate the pressure on the peseta.

"The drawback of small cuts is that they won't stop the upward pressure on the peseta but the Bank of Spain doesn't have any alternative. The Bank of Spain's target for inflation is 2.5 percent for the year."
"I expect January inflation to slow toward 2.9 percent."
CARMEN HERNANSANZ, MERRILL LYNCH MADRID

"I would emphasise the favourable evolution of underlying inflation that has fallen over the whole year 1.8 points to 3.0 percent. The fact that the number was expected doesn't take away any of its merit as a good figure. The perspectives continue to be very positive and there could be a stepwise effect in January given that there is no rise but a drop in some prices like those of utilities."
"The Bank of Spain has room to lower rates, but I believe that it will give itself time to seek the CPI data for January."
--Madrid Newsroom +34 1 585 2167
